newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares fall back at close on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares fall back at close on profit-taking.

text.p: Italian shares closed mixed on Monday after a surge in the morning on hopes of a breakthrough at an EU summit in Amsterdam followed by a sell-off when EU finance ministers announced agreement on a stability pact.

The all-share Mibtel index closed almost unchanged, easing 0.05 percent to 12,754 while the blue chip MIB30 also finished level at 19,282. Turnover dropped to 1.296 trillion lire from 2.097 trillion lire on Friday.
Stet and Telecom Italia, set for merger in the coming weeks, made headway but insurers were heavily sold after Friday's buying frenzy.

Fiat gained 1.74 percent to 6,140 lire, spurred by chairman Cesare Romiti's announcement at the annual shareholders' meeting that group sales are on course to rise around 15 percent in 1997 from the previous year.
But Fiat Managing Director Paolo Cantarella warned that car sales would drop back to 1997 levels if the government phased out a car incentive scheme later this year.
Among insurers, Generali was 1.28 percent lower at 29,823 lire, RAS was 2.15 percent off at 13,705 lire but Toro gained 1.96 percent, against the trend, closing at 19,271 lire.
